name: N Street Village
rationale: Closest model match: housing, health and recovery services for homeless and low-income women in DC; about 2x Calvary's revenue

name: House of Ruth (DC)
rationale: Housing and services for women, children and families in DC, including DV survivors; large comparator ($20M)

name: Open Arms Housing
rationale: Permanent supportive housing for women experiencing homelessness, with a mental-health focus; small ($2.5M), 77% government

name: New Endeavors by Women
rationale: Transitional housing for homeless women in DC; similar size ($3.1M); 82% government

name: District Alliance for Safe Housing (DASH)
rationale: Safe housing for DV and sexual-violence survivors in DC; Calvary's New Foundations site is also DV-designated; 90% government

name: My Sister's Place
rationale: DC DV shelter and housing for survivors and children; similar size ($8.3M)

name: DC SAFE
rationale: DV crisis response and emergency shelter in DC; OVSJG-funded like Calvary; 94% government

name: Samaritan Inns
rationale: Recovery-oriented housing for homeless adults in DC; similar size ($6.2M) but only 11% government (contrast case)

name: Christ House
rationale: Medical respite for people experiencing homelessness in DC; nearly identical revenue to Calvary ($4.9M)

name: Everyone Home DC
rationale: DC homelessness prevention and housing; nearly identical revenue ($4.9M); 85% government

name: Coalition for the Homeless
rationale: DC shelter and housing provider with women's programs; similar size ($7.5M); 92% government

name: Thrive DC
rationale: DC homelessness services, including a women's program; small ($2.6M) and almost entirely private (contrast case)

name: Miriam's Kitchen
rationale: Chronic homelessness and PSH case management in DC; philanthropy-led (10% government) with a large donor base

name: Community of Hope
rationale: Ward 8-based homelessness and health provider in Calvary's service area; large ($57.6M)

name: Covenant House Washington DC
rationale: Ward 8 shelter and crisis services (youth); similar size ($7.3M); same ward-level funders

name: Doorways for Women and Families
rationale: Arlington VA: women, families and DV survivors experiencing homelessness; closest suburban analog ($6.1M)

name: House of Ruth Maryland
rationale: Baltimore MD: DV services and housing for women and children; regional DV funder overlap ($11.6M)

name: Heartly House
rationale: Frederick MD: DV and sexual-assault shelter and services; similar size ($5.1M)
